speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to understand the extent of your bleeding issues to help diagnose your condition. Can you describe when these symptoms started and if you have noticed any bruising or bleeding from other sites, such as your gums?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any recent viral infections, fever, or unintentional weight loss? I also need to know if there is a family history of bleeding disorders or if the child has received any vaccinations recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Pneumonia does not cause petechiae or mucosal bleeding, so that diagnosis is incorrect. I need to rule out serious hematologic conditions, so please allow me to examine the child for hepatosplenomegaly and lymphadenopathy. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Peripheral Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the platelet count is normal, we must investigate a qualitative platelet defect or a coagulation factor deficiency. Have you noticed any bleeding from the umbilical stump at birth, or does the family have a history of hemophilia or other bleeding disorders? REQUEST TEST: Bleeding Time, PT, aPTT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding Time: Prolonged. PT: 12 seconds (normal). aPTT: 30 seconds (normal).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and coagulation times but a prolonged bleeding time, this points strongly toward a platelet function defect. I would like to examine the child's mouth for characteristic palatal petechiae and check for any signs of von Willebrand disease, such as a family history of mild bleeding. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity: Normal. ELISA Binding Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results showing deficient GIIb/IIIa receptors confirm the diagnosis of Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
